title: Four takeaways from Mark Zuckerberg’s massive AI manifesto
slides: Zuckerberg's AI manifesto: what does he really want?
He plans open-source artificial general intelligence, not just chatbots.
Yet his massive compute procurement could centralize power dangerously.
Your AI strategy should watch open-source models, not just APIs.
Test Meta's openly available models against your current stack.
thread_text:
1. The AI power play

Open-source AGI from Meta could hand superintelligence to anyone—but building it means centralizing control over the world's compute.

2. Compute is the new oil

Zuckerberg's plan to buy hundreds of thousands of GPUs creates a bottleneck—only he and a few giants can afford this, making open-source a facade.

3. The hidden twist

Open weights don't equal open power. If Meta keeps the training data and compute secret, the model's behavior stays under their thumb.

4. What it means for you

APIs lock you in—but open models let you own your stack. Yet, running them requires infrastructure you may not have. Weigh the trade-off.

5. Your next move

Take a prompt from your current workflow and run it on Meta's Llama 3. Compare the output. Does it match? Test it today.

instagram.caption:
Meta is buying hundreds of thousands of GPUs for open-source AGI—while promising the result will be free for everyone. That's a lot of power concentrated in one place. 🏭

The catch: open weights don't mean open control. If Meta keeps training data and compute secret, the model's behavior stays under their thumb. Anyone can download it, but nobody can truly audit it.

For you, this shifts the API-vs-open-model trade-off. APIs lock you into a vendor, but running open models requires infrastructure you may not have.

Take one prompt from your current workflow and run it on Meta's Llama 3 today. Does the output match your standards? That's your answer. 🧪
